properties.name: Project.domain is written and never read — but a framework registry is probably the wrong fix
properties.statement:
REASSESSED 2026-07-28, same day, on Anthony's instruction not to treat reflow's workflows as canon. This was first written as "which modelling framework is in use must be a recorded choice", arguing from reflow's framework_registry.json. On re-reading, the DEFECT is real and the PRIOR ART's solution is doubtful; the name has been changed to say so.

THE DEFECT, which stands on its own: Project.domain is free text, written by genesis, and read by nothing — it is on the write-only list from the 2026-07-28 sweep. reflow2's own Project carries domain = 'software'. Either something should read it or it should not be collected, and that is true regardless of what reflow did.

WHY reflow's ANSWER IS PROBABLY WRONG, stated plainly because the first version of this node treated it as the model to copy. (1) The terminology mapping is largely COSMETIC. framework_registry.json maps node to 'service' / 'gene' / 'agent' / 'species' and edge to 'interface' / 'interaction' / 'relationship' over one universal graph. Renaming the same structure does not change what can be computed about it, and it introduces a translation layer between what the user says and what the graph holds — a layer that can drift, and that every reader must now traverse. (2) The load-bearing claim is a SMELL, not a feature. reflow's LESSON-01 says "framework choice determines which NetworkX analyses are available". Analyses should be available based on WHAT THE GRAPH CONTAINS, not on a declared label: a cycle detector should run wherever there are dependency edges, whoever calls them interfaces or interactions. Gating capability on a self-declared category is how a user gets the wrong answer for a reason they cannot see. reflow2's one universal vocabulary with computations keyed to STRUCTURE is very likely the better design, and adopting a registry would be a regression dressed as a feature.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM reflow: only the rule, and reflow2 already has it. LESSON-01's real content — "Do NOT default to UAF" — is req:defaults-do-not-assert, independently arrived at. The supporting CONTRADICTS edge to that requirement stays correct; the framework registry is not the mechanism it implies.

WHAT SHOULD ACTUALLY BE DECIDED, and it is smaller than a registry: does anything read Project.domain, and if not, does it become unspecified-until-stated (per ver:interface-spec's rule for Interface.medium) or leave the schema entirely? A plausible middle path worth weighing separately: domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing — what vocabulary the agent uses when talking to the user and reading their documents — without ever gating which computations run. That keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services') and discards the part that would make analyses conditional on a label. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 00b-framework_selection.json; reassessed the same day.
